Get our local guides and events updates.

This guide covers 17 performing arts venues and companies in Chattanooga. Items span theatre, dance, symphony, and comedy.
The Tivoli Foundation operates three downtown venues: the Tivoli Theatre, Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium, and Walker Theatre. The Tivoli Theatre reopened October 20, 2026 after a four-year, $75 million restoration. It had been dark since 2022. Billy Strings played the first two sold-out shows back.
UTC’s Fine Arts Center is the city’s second major performance hub. The Chattanooga Ballet, Chattanooga Dance Theatre, and UTC Theatre Co. all stage productions there. The Chattanooga Symphony & Opera is back at the restored Tivoli for the 2026-27 season.
The Genre filter separates venues by type. Dance finds three companies. Concert Venue surfaces the four large halls that host touring acts. The Kids filter returns seven entries with family-friendly programming.
December is the busiest month. Both Chattanooga Ballet and Chattanooga Dance Theatre stage Nutcracker productions. The Tivoli’s holiday programming also runs then. Buy tickets in October for the best seats.
If there is a performance company worth adding, send an email. Details change. Confirm before you go.

Theatre in Chattanooga.

Eleven theatre companies and venues appear in this filter. The Tivoli Foundation anchors the downtown scene with three historic buildings. Community companies include Chattanooga Theatre Centre, Ensemble Theatre, UTC Theatre Co., and several neighborhood troupes. Two companies perform outdoors seasonally: Scenic City Shakespeare at Greenway Farms and Signal Mountain Playhouse.

Live music guideMuseums and exhibits

Family-Friendly Performances.

Seven venues in this guide offer family-friendly programming. Chattanooga Theatre Centre and UTC Theatre Co. run year-round shows with accessible ticket prices. The Nooga Nutcracker at UTC in December is a local tradition. Scenic City Shakespeare at Greenway Farms is free and brings families outdoors in spring and fall. Chattanooga Ballet fills Memorial Auditorium with 200+ dancers each December for the Nutcracker.

Museums and exhibits

Downtown Chattanooga Venues.

Six venues in this filter are in or near downtown. The Tivoli Theatre, Memorial Auditorium, and Walker Theatre are all operated by the Tivoli Foundation and within two blocks of each other. Bessie Smith Cultural Center is a 10-minute walk east on MLK Blvd. Comedy Catch on Station Street is a 10-minute walk south on Broad Street. UTC Theatre and the Fine Arts Center anchor the eastern end of the downtown corridor.

Downtown live musicDowntown coffee

Northside Chattanooga.

Chattanooga Theatre Centre and Chattanooga Ballet are both on the North Shore next to Coolidge Park. Barking Legs Theater is a few minutes east in Highland Park on Dodds Avenue. These three are the best reasons to cross the river for a performance night. All three are within a short drive of each other.

1. Tivoli Theatre .

Historic Beaux-Arts venue on Broad Street in downtown Chattanooga. It opened in 1921 and is known as the Jewel of the South. The theatre closed in 2022 for a four-year, $75 million restoration and reopened October 20, 2026. Billy Strings played the first two sold-out shows. The adjacent Fowler Brothers building now houses the new Bobby Stone Theatre. Broadway tours, concerts, comedy, and film series all run here. Find the full calendar at tivolichattanooga.com.

2. Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Auditorium .

Downtown venue dedicated in 1922 to Hamilton County's armed forces. Holds up to 3,866 people. Hosts concerts, comedy headliners, and community events. While the Tivoli was under restoration, most Tivoli Foundation shows ran here. Some symphony and touring acts still perform here alongside Tivoli shows. Part of the Tivoli Foundation. Find the schedule at tivolichattanooga.com.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #concert-venue #comedy #downtown

3. Walker Theatre .

Intimate 851-seat performance space inside the same building as Memorial Auditorium on McCallie Ave. Known for strong acoustics and a charming layout. Hosts smaller touring productions and specialty shows. Part of the Tivoli Foundation. Find the schedule at tivolichattanooga.com.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #concert-venue #downtown

4. Chattanooga Symphony & Opera .

Professional orchestra and opera company performing at the restored Tivoli Theatre and Soldiers & Sailors Memorial. A season can include Rachmaninoff, Handel's Messiah, pops nights, and live film scores. The CSO has played the Star Wars scores live to picture in recent seasons. Buy tickets online or call the box office at (423) 267-8583.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #symphony #downtown

5. Chattanooga Theatre Centre .

Community theatre on the North Shore next to Coolidge Park and the Tennessee River. One of the oldest and largest community theatres in the US, over 100 years old. New productions run every 6-8 weeks, usually Thursday through Sunday. Past shows include Matilda the Musical, Fences, and A Raisin in the Sun. Free parking is on site but fills fast on weekends. Arrive 15-20 minutes early.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #kids #northside

6. Scenic City Shakespeare .

Free outdoor Shakespeare at Greenway Farms in Hixson. Two productions per year, typically in spring and fall on Friday and Saturday evenings. No tickets or reservations needed. Past shows include Othello, Macbeth, and A Midsummer Night's Dream. Bring a lawn chair, blankets, and snacks. Finding the outdoor stage has tripped up first-timers - check the aerial visual on their website.
Google Maps Website
#outdoor #theatre #free #affordable #seasonal #kids #hixson

7. Barking Legs Theater .

Small eclectic venue just off Dodds Avenue in Highland Park. Hosts contemporary dance, experimental jazz, poetry slams, singer-songwriters, film nights, and storytelling. Most tickets are under $20. Shows run year-round on weekend evenings. The calendar updates based on performer availability. Check barkinglegs.org for the current schedule.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #dance #affordable #northside

8. Chattanooga Ballet .

Professional dance company and school based on North Market Street on the North Shore. Bigger productions land at UTC's Fine Arts Center. Each December the Nutcracker fills Memorial Auditorium with more than 200 dancers. In 2027, they bring Curveball to the Tivoli - a ballet about Chattanooga pitcher Jackie Mitchell, who struck out Babe Ruth. The school takes students age three and up. Buy tickets at chaballet.org or call (423) 265-0617.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #dance #kids #northside

9. Chattanooga Dance Theatre .

Hixson-based studio and company behind the Nooga Nutcracker. The show is a local spin on the classic - the Tennessee River, aquarium fish, and the Lookouts replace the usual cast. Staged each December at UTC's Roland Hayes Concert Hall. Features 60+ performers mixing ballet, jazz, modern, and acrobatics. Tickets go on sale each October through the UTC box office.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #dance #kids #seasonal #hixson

10. The Comedy Catch .

Dedicated comedy club on Station Street in the Southside entertainment district. Shows run every night with touring headliners and local showcases. The Wednesday open mic is the longest-running in the city. Some events are family-friendly - check the listing for an indicator before you go. A $5 minimum food or drink purchase applies per person. Host of the annual Lookout Comedy Festival each fall.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #comedy #southside

11. Improv Chattanooga .

Local improv troupe performing at rotating venues around the city. Past shows have landed at the library after hours, Barking Legs, and coffee shops in Cleveland. Ticket prices vary by show. Free classes run regularly. The troupe can also be hired for private events. Find upcoming shows at improvchattanooga.com.
Website
#indoor #comedy #affordable

12. Ensemble Theatre of Chattanooga .

Year-round production company focused on contemporary and socially conscious plays. New productions run every six to eight weeks. Past seasons included short play festivals in January-February and musical concerts in summer. Find the current schedule at ensembletheatreofchattanooga.com.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #affordable

13. UTC Theatre Co. .

University of Tennessee at Chattanooga stages four public productions per year at the Dorothy Hackett Ward Theatre in the Fine Arts Center. Past shows include Shakespeare, new plays, and spring musicals like Big Fish. Tickets are affordable and the public is welcome. Browse the season at utc.edu.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #theatre #kids #affordable #downtown

14. Bessie Smith Cultural Center .

Performance hall and museum at 200 E Martin Luther King Blvd. Named for Chattanooga native and Empress of the Blues Bessie Smith. The hall hosts concerts, community events, and an annual legacy gala. The adjacent museum covers African American history in Chattanooga. Details at bessiesmithcc.org.
Google Maps Website
#indoor #concert-venue #downtown

15. Back Alley Productions .

Nonprofit theatre company based in LaFayette, GA, about 25 minutes from Chattanooga. Performs at the Historic Mars Theatre with a full season of plays and musicals. Shows run mostly fall through spring, with dates shifting each year. Voted Best Live Performance Venue in North Georgia 2018-2020.
Google Maps

16. Signal Mountain Playhouse .

Community theatre on Signal Mountain with two productions per year. The summer outdoor musical runs in July on Friday and Saturday evenings. The winter indoor show lands around February at the Mountain Arts Community Center. Programming is family-friendly. Find show details on their Facebook page.
Google Maps Website

17. East Brainerd Community Theater .

Community theatre based at Christ United Methodist Church on East Brainerd Road. Typically stages one play and one musical per year. The summer musical is usually a large production with a full cast. Past shows include The Music Man, Pirates of Penzance, and Guys and Dolls. Find details at ebctchatt.com.

The three Tivoli Foundation venues are within two blocks of each other downtown. Check whether your show is at the Tivoli Theatre, Memorial Auditorium, or Walker Theatre before you go. Each has a different entrance and capacity.
December runs hot for dance. Both the Chattanooga Ballet Nutcracker and the Nooga Nutcracker run then, and the Chattanooga Symphony’s holiday shows sell fast. Buy tickets in October for the best seats.
For live music at smaller bars and listening rooms, see the live music guide. Barking Legs sits between the two categories - intimate performances that don’t fit neatly in either.

FAQ.

What Broadway shows come to Chattanooga?

Broadway touring productions typically come to the Tivoli Theatre on Broad Street, operated by the Tivoli Foundation. The Tivoli reopened October 2026 after a four-year, $75 million restoration. It now includes an expanded performance center in the adjacent Fowler Brothers building. Check tivolichattanooga.com for the current season lineup.

Where can I see free live theatre in Chattanooga?

Scenic City Shakespeare performs free outdoor productions at Greenway Farms in Hixson, typically in spring and fall on Friday and Saturday evenings. No tickets or reservations are required. Bring a lawn chair and snacks. Check sceniccityshakespeare.org for the next production date.

What are the best family-friendly performances in Chattanooga?

Seven venues in this guide offer family-friendly programming. In December, both Chattanooga Ballet and Chattanooga Dance Theatre stage Nutcracker productions. Chattanooga Theatre Centre runs family musicals and youth shows year-round on the North Shore. Scenic City Shakespeare is free and outdoor. UTC Theatre Co. stages affordable public shows four times a year.

Does the Chattanooga Symphony play anything besides classical music?

Yes. The Chattanooga Symphony and Opera runs pops programming alongside the classical season. They have played live film scores in past seasons, including the Star Wars scores performed live to picture. Check chattanoogasymphony.org for the current season.

What is the Nooga Nutcracker?

The Nooga Nutcracker is a Chattanooga-specific spin on the classic ballet, staged by Chattanooga Dance Theatre each December at UTC’s Roland Hayes Concert Hall. It replaces the standard characters with local stand-ins: the Tennessee River, aquarium fish, and the Chattanooga Lookouts. It features 60+ performers. Tickets go on sale in October through the UTC box office.
